name: mummer
summary: MUMmer 3.23 mummer (maxmat3): the maximal exact matches between a reference and query files, in the program's order.
short: MUMmer mummer: maximal exact matches (-mum / -mumreference / -maxmatch, -n -l -b -r -s -c -F -L), byte for byte.
description: MUMmer 3.23 mummer (Kurtz' maxmat3): the maximal exact matches between a reference file and one or more query files. matchMode 'mumreference' (default) reports matches unique in the reference, 'mum' matches unique in both, 'maxmatch' every maximal match; minLength = -l (default 20); nucleotidesOnly (-n) matches only a, c, g, t (any case); both (-b) adds the reverse-complement strand of the query, reverseOnly (-r) only that strand. Output per query record: a '> id' line and one line per match: reference position, query position, length (with several reference records or fourColumn = -F the reference id is the first column), followed by the matching text with showString (-s). Byte for byte equal to the installed mummer on 3 200 random runs (every mode, every option, multi-record files, N / IUPAC / odd characters, CR LF).

text: What mummer writes to standard output.
messages: The deterministic lines of standard error ('# reading input file ...'; the timing lines are left out).

errors: Sequence cannot be null or empty
At least one query file is required
mummer: empty sequence in multiple fasta file
mummer: option -b and option -r exclude each other

example.title: Maximal unique matches on both strands
example.prompt: Find the maximal unique matches of length >= 8 on both strands.

output.text:
> q
       1        14        20
acgtacgtacgtaaccggtt
> q Reverse
       1        10        13
acgtacgtacgta
      12         1         9
taaccggtt
output.messages:
# reading input file "reference.fa" of length 20
# construct suffix tree for sequence of length 20
# (maximum reference length is 536870908)
# (maximum query length is 4294967295)
# reading input file "query.fa" of length 34
# matching query-file "query.fa"
# against subject-file "reference.fa"

example.note: mummer -mum -l 8 -b -s r.fa q.fa: the whole reference matches the query at 14; the reverse-complement strand matches twice (the positions are in the reverse-complemented query).
